name: Gao & Wald, 'Theorems on gravitational time delay and related issues', CQG 17, 4999 (2000), gr-qc/0007021v2: Theorem 1 (fastest null geodesics avoid compact sets), Theorem 2 (asymptotically-AdS time delay), eq.(13) focusing equation with shear

source.located: arXiv gr-qc/0007021v2 (28 Jul 2000), full text, all 15 pages incl. Theorem 1, Lemma 1, Corollary 1, Theorem 2, eqs.(1)-(18), footnotes 1-3, refs [1]-[15]

published_statement: THEOREM 1 (p.6): 'Let (M,g_ab) be a null geodesically complete spacetime satisfying the null energy condition (2) and the null generic condition (see eq.(9)). Then given any compact region K in M, there exists another compact region K' containing K such that if q,p not in K' and q in J+(p) - I+(p), then any causal curve gamma connecting p to q cannot intersect the region K.' The authors' own gloss (p.5 and p.10): 'the theorem suggests that "time advance" is not possible, although it is difficult to make a strong argument for this interpretation, since the theorem gives little control over the size of the region K''. THEOREM 2 (p.12-13): for (M,g) conformally embeddable with a timelike conformal boundary, NEC + null generic, strongly causal closure, J+(p)∩J-(q) compact: any causal curve between p and q in the boundary of A(p) lies entirely in the boundary -- interpreted (p.14) as 'the propagation of light through an asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime will always be "delayed" relative to propagation through anti-de Sitter spacetime itself', the comparison being well defined only because the boundary geometry is held fixed. EQ.(13) (p.7): with A^mu_nu from eq.(11) (d^2A/dlambda^2 = -sum R_{alpha beta sigma}^mu k^alpha k^sigma A^beta_nu, A|p = 0, dA/dlambda|p = delta) and G = sqrt(det A) (eq.12), 'the Raychaudhuri equation yields (see e.g. [10]) G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b]'. INTRODUCTION (pp.2-4): the Visser-Bassett-Liberati linearised result h_ab k^a k^b >= 0 [their ref 3 = gr-qc/9810026, gr-qc/9908023] 'is highly gauge dependent'; eqs.(6)-(8) give a smooth pure-gauge h_ab, O(1/r) at infinity, that 'opens out the light cones everywhere', so 'we can reverse the conclusions of [3] in any compact region of spacetime'; 'in general, there is no natural way to choose a flat background for a curved spacetime, and, thus, no meaningful way to compare the propagation of a light ray in a curved spacetime with that of a "corresponding" light ray in Minkowski spacetime'; Olum's result is cited as applying to spacetimes Minkowskian outside a world tube, which the DEC + positive mass theorem permit only for Minkowski itself.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Thm 1, Thm 2, Lemma 1) null energy condition R_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for all null k (eq.2) -- stated geometrically on Ricci, not on T_ab; Thm 2 footnote 3: NEC replaceable by Borde's averaged condition
H2 (Thm 1, Thm 2) null generic condition: every null geodesic contains a point with k_[a R_b]cd[e k_f] k^c k^d != 0 (eq.9)
H3 (Thm 1) null geodesic completeness; footnote 1 (Galloway): H1+H2+H3 may be replaced by the single hypothesis 'M contains no null line'

H4 (Thm 1) conclusion holds only for p,q outside a compact K' that the theorem does not bound -- an asymptotic statement about fastest null geodesics between far-separated events, with no comparison to any reference geometry

H5 (Thm 2) conformal embedding with timelike boundary (asymptotically AdS prototype), strong causality of the closure, compactness of causal diamonds; the 'delay' is relative to boundary null geodesics with the boundary geometry fixed
H6 (all) connected, smooth, time-oriented, paracompact; no dimension assumed ('our results hold in any spacetime dimension'); no staticity, symmetry or asymptotic flatness assumed

H7 (eq.13) null geodesic congruence from a point (twist-free), affine parameter; the Raychaudhuri equation as input (quoted from ref [10], Flanagan-Marolf-Wald hep-th/9908070, not derived in the paper)
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H2 and H3 (and Galloway's no-null-line replacement) -- driven.py:116-118 states Theorem 1 as 'the NEC makes Shapiro always a delay, never an advance' with 'no staticity hypothesis'; foliation.py:237-239 ('with the NEC, never an advance'). Theorem 1 needs NEC AND null generic AND null geodesic completeness. Machine-checked here (rederive F1): on the RADIAL null rays that foliation.py section 8 times (10M -> 100M, foliation.py:305-313), the null generic quantity vanishes identically at every sampled r (3,10,50,100 M) because radial is a principal null direction of Schwarzschild; and Schwarzschild is not null geodesically complete. The example the tree says the theorem explains lies outside the theorem's hypotheses.

ADDED a reference-geometry comparison -- foliation.py:235-239 (D4 'arrives EARLIER than in the reference geometry ... THE THEOREM IS REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE ... Gao & Wald'), foliation.py:613-614 ('D4 arrival earlier than the reference geometry' -> 'REPLACED BY A STRONGER ONE -- Olum, Gao-Wald, VBL'). Gao-Wald Theorem 1 makes NO comparison with a reference geometry; the paper's stated purpose (p.4) is theorems that 'do not require a comparison with Minkowski spacetime'. The only reference comparison in the paper is Theorem 2, and it needs a timelike conformal boundary with fixed boundary geometry (asymptotically AdS), not an asymptotically flat corridor.

INVERTED the paper's position on the companion citation -- foliation.py:314-317 'Gao & Wald and Visser-Bassett-Liberati say the sign of that excess is forced by the NEC'; driven.py:116-118 groups them. Gao-Wald's introduction argues the VBL light-cone result is gauge dependent and reversible in any compact region by a pure gauge (eqs.6-8, machine-checked here as rederive E1/E2), and that comparing a curved-spacetime arrival with a flat one has 'no natural' meaning. Gao-Wald do not say the sign of the Schwarzschild Killing-time excess is forced by anything; they cite Penrose's theorem that Schwarzschild cannot be identified with Minkowski with coinciding null infinities and Schwarzschild cones inside Minkowski's (an 'anti-time-delay' reading they attribute to the identification, not to gravity).

WEAKENED the authors' own interpretive caveat -- the tree calls Theorem 1 'standing' (driven.py:116) and 'stronger' than D4 (foliation.py:237, 614) as a no-advance theorem; the authors write 'it is difficult to make a strong argument for this interpretation' (pp.5, 10).
HELD (no drift) -- 'no staticity' (driven.py:116-117, foliation.py:316-317): correct, neither theorem assumes staticity or any symmetry (H6).

HELD (no drift) for eq.(13) as used -- composite.py:18-20 quotes G''/G = -(1/2)[sigma_ab sigma^ab + R_ab k^a k^b] verbatim with the correct equation number; composite.py:36-40 evolves a 2x2 parallel-propagated screen in 4D, which is exactly the domain where eq.(13) is an identity (rederive A2, C1).

OWNER READING, NOT GAO-WALD -- composite.py:24-29 'WEYL focusing sigma^2 QUADRATIC in the source ... SIGN-BLIND ... exactly as hard' is not stated in the paper (the canonical entry already flags this). Checked here (rederive C2): in the straight-ray Born approximation T(-M) is T(M) with the transverse axes swapped, so conjugate points coincide exactly (55.8658 for both signs; thin-lens 55.652); composite.py's own docstring records 55.16 vs 56.52 (2.47 % apart), so 'exactly as hard' (composite.py:28) holds at first order in M only, which the selftest's 0.05 tolerance (composite.py:359-360) already encodes. A statement-precision point for the owner, not a drift from the source.

NOT DRIFT BUT A SOURCE DISCREPANCY composite.py inherits nothing from -- eq.(13) read literally (A the full n x n matrix of eq.11, G = sqrt(det A), 'any spacetime dimension') is not an identity: det A = lambda^2 det A_perp (rederive B2) and flat space gives G = lambda^2, G'' = 2 > 0 against RHS 0 (B1); in n dims the coefficient 1/2 is n=4-specific (A3: residual (n-4)(n-2)D'^2/(4D^2)). The correct object is G = (det A_perp)^(1/(n-2)) with coefficient 1/(n-2) (A1). Lemma 1's proof needs only a concave function vanishing at conjugate points, which that object supplies, so the theorem is untouched. Recorded as a notational discrepancy, NOT an error in the result (fluctuation.py precedent).

later_literature.ref: Page, Surya & Woolgar, 'Positive mass from holographic causality', PRL 89 (2002) 121301, hep-th/0204198
later_literature.what: Remark (ii): positivity of mass does NOT imply non-negative time delay ('by choosing gamma and gamma' suitably, the time delay could be made negative'); non-negative bulk-vs-boundary delay follows from null genericity + null geodesic completeness + NEC via the focusing theorem -- i.e. the generic and completeness hypotheses are load-bearing, exactly the ones the tree drops. Also: the negative-mass AdS soliton still has strictly positive delay, so sign of mass and sign of delay are not tied in general.

later_literature.ref: Paternain & Woolgar, 'Conformal boundary rigidity from null geodesic travel times', arXiv:2606.28689v3 (2026)
later_literature.what: Rigidity case of the time-delay/positive-mass link: under NEC in 4D (or staticity, or stationarity) an asymptotically AdS spacetime with no delay for any boundary-to-boundary null geodesic is AdS; asymptotically flat analogue (Prop. 5.4) under NEC. Remark 5.3(2): spacetimes approaching negative-mass Schwarzschild outside a tube exist, violate energy conditions, and fail the null boundary Penrose property -- the regime of composite.py's negative mass lies outside every theorem of this family.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. Gao-Wald's theorems take no empirical input (H1-H7 are geometric), so no datum the authors lacked can move them: the Cassini 2003 improvement of the Shapiro test by ~50x over Viking (Will arXiv:1403.7377, READ) confirms GR's solar delay but is not an input. What the authors lacked in 2000 was later MATHEMATICS, and it moved in their favour or extended them: Galloway's footnote-1 strengthening (no null line suffices); Page-Surya-Woolgar 2002 (holographic causality version, and explicit confirmation that the generic+completeness+NEC route is what gives non-negative delay); Paternain-Woolgar 2026 (rigidity). The only thing that is 'incomplete' here is on the tree's side: the tree cites Theorem 1 for a claim (NEC alone => no advance against a reference geometry, including Schwarzschild radial transit) that the paper does not make and whose central obstacle (no invariant reference identification; VBL's result reversible by gauge) the paper itself demonstrates. Evidence against M's hypothesis for THIS result: re-derivation reproduces every checkable step (eq.7, eq.8, eq.13 in 4D); the one discrepancy found (literal n x n reading of eqs.11-13, and '1/2' in 'any dimension') is notational and leaves the proof valid with G = (det A_perp)^(1/(n-2)).
grade_evidence: The source STANDS as published (Theorems 1-2 re-read in full; eqs.7-8 and eq.13 in 4D machine-checked; no counterexample; one notational discrepancy in the literal n-dimensional reading of eqs.11-13 that does not affect the proof). The TREE's use is NARROWED: (a) driven.py:116-118 and foliation.py:237-239, 314-317, 613-614 drop the null generic condition and null geodesic completeness and add a reference-geometry comparison the theorem does not contain; the example foliation.py attaches it to (Schwarzschild radial transit, foliation.py:305-317) violates the null generic hypothesis on every sampled point of the ray (rederive F1) and is null-incomplete; the paper argues against the VBL flat-comparison reading the tree pairs it with (eqs.6-8, rederive E1/E2). (b) composite.py's use of eq.(13) is within the source's valid domain (4D, 2x2 screen; rederive A2, C1) and stands; composite.py's 'sign-blind / exactly as hard' is the owner's first-order reading, confirmed at O(M) in the Born approximation (C2) and not claimed by Gao-Wald. Nothing in (a) or (b) is a refutation of the paper; (a) is a statement the paper does not support, so the tree's 'standing ... never an advance' may not be attributed to gr-qc/0007021 as written.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS for the foliation/driven use: restate the citation with Theorem 1's actual hypotheses (NEC + null generic + null geodesic completeness, or no null line) and conclusion (fastest null geodesics between far events avoid any compact set), drop 'Shapiro always a delay' and the reference-geometry comparison, or cite Theorem 2 only for asymptotically-AdS spacetimes with fixed boundary geometry; for the Schwarzschild-excess sign cite a result that covers radial rays of a null-incomplete, non-generic spacetime (Gao-Wald do not). To WRONG: a spacetime satisfying H1-H3 with a fastest null geodesic between arbitrarily far p,q entering a fixed compact K -- none known, and the proof re-checks. To OPEN: none; the paper is READ in full.
